item.title: This week on "Sunday Morning" (Oct. 25)
item.description: A look at the features for this week's broadcast of the Emmy-winning program, hosted by Jane Pauley.

item.title: David Sedaris would like to clear the air about prostate exams
item.description: After a friend divulged perhaps too much information, humorist David Sedaris considers the ramifications of over-sharing – and wrong assumptions.

item.title: How punk rock and MTV inspired opera composer Missy Mazzoli
item.description: "Lincoln in the Bardo," based on George Saunders' novel, is the first opera composed by a woman to premiere at the Metropolitan Opera. Missy Mazzoli talks about its creation, and the influence that punk rock and music videos had on her work.

item.title: "Lincoln in the Bardo" composer Missy Mazzoli
item.description: Composer Missy Mazzoli is the first woman ever to have an opera premiered by the Metropolitan Opera. Based on the award-winning novel by George Saunders, Mazzoli and librettist Royce Vavrek's "Lincoln in the Bardo" depicts Abraham Lincoln mourning his 11-year-old son, Willie, whose passing has led the young boy to a threshold place between the living and the dead. Correspondent Faith Salie talks with Mazzoli about the opera and the influence that punk rock and music videos had on her work.

item.title: Photos of the week
item.description: "Sunday Morning" looks at some of the most evocative images captured the week of Oct. 18-24, 2026.

item.title: "The Mosquito Bowl" and the human cost of war
item.description: Director Peter Berg discusses his new film, the true story of All-American football stars who volunteered for the Marines and fought in the Battle of Okinawa, the last and costliest World War II battle in the Pacific.

item.title: "The Mosquito Bowl" and the human cost of war
item.description: The new Netflix film "The Mosquito Bowl" recounts the true story of All-American football stars who volunteered for the Marines following Pearl Harbor – and fought in the Battle of Okinawa, the last and costliest World War II battle in the Pacific. CBS News national security correspondent David Martin talks with director Peter Berg ("Friday Night Lights") about translating the story of young men trained for war to the screen.

item.title: At least 12 injured, including 6 children, in shooting near Florida A&M
item.description: Police say a fight broke out before the shooting.

item.title: Twin doctors on their climb out of poverty
item.description: Drs. Travan and Travis Jasper, identical twins, are co-directors of the emergency department at Chippenham Hospital in Richmond, Virginia. Their path to heading the ER started when they were 12, during a hospital visit experience that motivated them to achieve something greater. Steve Hartman talks with the Jasper twins about turning trauma into triumph, and helplessness into healing.

item.title: Meet the Tower of London's Ravenmaster
item.description: Legend warns that if the ravens leave London's Tower of London, the monument would crumble – as would the British monarchy. And so, they are kept, a well-fed draw for tourists. Correspondent Seth Doane meets the man charged with caring for these feathered protectors of the realm.

item.title: Parker Posey: "I have felt in the right place at the right time"
item.description: In the 1990s actress Parker Posey was dubbed "The Queen of the Indies." The Emmy-nominated star of "The White Lotus," and the new film "Wild Horse Nine" talks about her Southern upbringing, and how her parents inspired her acting.

item.title: Passage: In memoriam
item.description: "Sunday Morning" remembers some of the notable figures who left us this week, including actor Tom Skerritt, known for such films as "Top Gun," "Alien," and "Steel Magnolias," and the TV series "Picket Fences."

item.title: Extended interview: Parker Posey
item.description: In this web exclusive, actress Parker Posey ("Party Girl," "The White Lotus," "Wild Horse Nine") talks with correspondent Mo Rocca about her movie and TV career, during which she was dubbed "Queen of the Indies."

item.title: The unforgettable Parker Posey
item.description: In the 1990s actress Parker Posey became a breakout star in independent films like "Party Girl," and was dubbed "The Queen of the Indies." Recently she earned an Emmy nomination for "The White Lotus," and is featured in the new Martin McDonagh film "Wild Horse Nine." She talks with correspondent (and fellow summer theater school classmate) Mo Rocca about her Southern upbringing, and how her parents inspired her acting.

item.title: Ghost signs: Fading reminders of the past
item.description: They're painted advertisements from long ago, for businesses that may have since died. But remnants of these "ghost signs" still remain, haunting our urban spaces – and one artist is bringing ghost signs back to life.

item.title: Ghost signs: Fading reminders of the past
item.description: They're painted advertisements from long ago, for businesses that may have since died. But remnants of these "ghost signs" still remain, haunting our urban spaces. Correspondent Conor Knighton talks with marketing expert Ronald Ladouceur about the origins of these outdoor ads; and with artist Craig Winslow, who is bringing ghost signs back to life.

item.title: Israeli election to test Netanyahu's ability to hold power
item.description: On Tuesday, Israel will hold its first parliamentary elections since the Oct. 7, 2023, terror attacks. Essentially one man is on the ballot: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. How might Israeli policy change if the opposition succeeds?

item.title: 100 years later, the mystery of Houdini's death endures
item.description: Harry Houdini, the greatest escape artist who ever lived, died 100 years ago on Halloween – a fact that has only burnished his image as a daredevil who often cheated death. But was there a cover-up involving the circumstances of his death?

item.title: Israeli election to test Benjamin Netanyahu's ability to hold power
item.description: On Tuesday, Israel will hold its first parliamentary elections since the October 7, 2023 terror attacks. Essentially one man is on the ballot: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. Matt Gutman reports from Tel Aviv on the divide over Netanyahu, and how Israeli policy might or might not change if the opposition succeeds.

item.title: Almanac: October 25
item.description: "Sunday Morning" looks back at historical events on this date.

item.title: The mystery of Houdini's death
item.description: Harry Houdini, the greatest escape artist who ever lived, died 100 years ago on Halloween – a fact that has only burnished his image as a daredevil who often cheated death. Correspondent David Pogue examines the life, and after-life, of a man who seemingly performed the impossible while also debunking seances and fake mystics; and looks into the mystery surrounding Houdini's death at age 52.

item.description: The U.S. ambassador to the U.N. says the war with Iran could last another year, but he hopes Tehran will "come to the table" sooner.

item.description: The North Korean leader used the trip to reaffirm ties with its powerful neighbor.

item.description: While demonstrations throughout France were largely peaceful, police reported clashes with protesters Saturday evening.

item.title: Man's murder, wife's death feed into local legend of "cursed" mansion
item.description: When Mike Harding, a California transplant, spotted a majestic mansion in Celina, Tennessee, he thought he'd found the dream retirement home for himself and his wife, Julie. But those dreams ended abruptly when Mike suddenly went missing in 2022.

item.description: Doral, Florida, has the largest Venezuelan population of any city in the country.

item.description: President Trump and the first lady voted in Florida before he jetted off to Georgia for a campaign rally.
